newsitem.title: CHINA: Daewoo to build skyscraper in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo to build skyscraper in Shanghai.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Corp will build a 92-storey office and hotel tower in Shanghai costing around $700 million to be completed in the year 2000, a Daewoo official said on Tuesday.
Jeon Byung-woo, Daewoo's chief representative in Shanghai, said his company had full confidence in Shanghai's future despite the current real estate glut in the city.
"We are Asians and we have strong confidence in the future of Shanghai," he said. "Right now real estate is not so good, but location is very important and this is one of the best in Shanghai."

The building, to be called the Shanghai Daewoo Business Centre, will be built on a prime site in the Xuhui area to the west of Shanghai's city centre and will have a floor area of four million square feet, a news release said.
It will feature a 92-storey office and hotel tower, which the release said would be the world's fifth tallest building, as well as a 37-storey apartmnent tower and a shopping centre.
The release said it was decided to make the main tower 92 storeys in height to symbolise the 1992 establishment of diplomatic relations between China and South Korea.
